key_insight: A multimodal graph neural network can reliably identify and prioritize cancer immunotherapy targets, and top computational candidates are validated using clinically relevant patient-derived tumour explants, linking in silico predictions to actionable biological evidence.
problem_solved: Addresses the gap between large-scale computational target nomination and clinically relevant validation by providing a model that both distinguishes approved vs prospective immunotherapy targets and routes promising predictions into a patient-derived experimental platform for validation.
method: Multimodal graph neural network that integrates diverse data types (e.g., molecular, pathway, and clinical/contextual features) into a graph representation of candidate targets.
Model trained to distinguish approved targets from prospective candidates and to rank or score novel targets by therapeutic potential.
Top-ranked predictions validated experimentally using a patient-derived tumour explant (PDTE) platform to confirm biological relevance in a clinically representative context.
impact: Demonstrates a practical AI-to-bench workflow: ML (multimodal GNNs) can accelerate target discovery and prioritization, while PDTE validation increases translational confidence—useful for ML practitioners aiming to produce experimentally actionable predictions.
visual_elements: Schematic of the multimodal GNN: input modalities (molecular, pathway, clinical) → graph construction → target scoring
Pipeline flowchart from model prediction to patient-derived tumour explant validation
Ranked candidate list or heatmap showing model scores with validation outcomes (approved, prospective, validated in explants)
Performance chart (e.g., precision/recall or enrichment of approved targets among top predictions)
paper_title: Immunotherapy drug target identification using machine learning and patient-derived tumour explant validation
paper_authors: Marcellus Augustine, Nuno Rocha Nene, Hongchang Fu, Christopher L. Pinder, Lorena Ligammari
